day-paper.purpose: Day print paper and the card faces (--paper).

day-paper-deep.purpose: Day print fields: the riddle input, the cake plate (--paper-deep).

graphite-ink.purpose: Day print ink: headings, links, frames, solid buttons (--ink).

day-rule.purpose: Day print dividers and the rules inside the card (--rule).

day-halftone.purpose: Day print halftone dots for baselines and test data (--halftone).

day-desk.purpose: The surface the card lies on in the day print (--desk).

meishi-red.purpose: Day print second drum: misregistration, fills, charts, underlines, focus (--accent, --focus).

day-on-accent.purpose: Text on red fills in the day print (--on-accent).

night-paper.purpose: Night print paper and card faces.

night-desk.purpose: The surface the card lies on in the night print.

night-red.purpose: Night print second drum and focus; brighter so it reads on dark stock.

night-on-accent.purpose: Text on red fills in the night print.

display.purpose: "The build log" on the cover; prints in at the end of the card flip. Misregistered 6px 4px (4px 3px on phones).

card-name.purpose: The name on the card's front, the page's h1. Misregistered 2px 2px.

headline.purpose: Section titles, always misregistered (.ink), printed in on scroll.

title.purpose: Project and role titles on a page.

body.purpose: Paragraphs and points, 65ch; italic in --muted for ledes, meta, captions and the colophon.

label.purpose: Masthead contents, toggle, folios, chart values, cover lines, contact links, card labels (Anybody 600 to 800).

shadows.name: misregistration
shadows.purpose: text-shadow: the red pass on .ink titles and the card name; 0 0 0 when in register.

shadows.name: card-shadow
shadows.purpose: --card-shadow (day; night uses black at .4 and .7): the name card on the desk. The only cast shadow.

shadows.name: ink-outline
shadows.purpose: Outline on chart result bars (1px --halftone on baselines).

shadows.name: fold-edge
shadows.purpose: Crease on the riddle's dog-eared corner.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Default easing for every response and the hand-over.

motion.name: hand-over
motion.purpose: Only automatic motion: the card rises from 44px down, tipped back 20deg, overshoots slightly (-6px, -5deg) and settles. Skipped for returning visitors (data-card="seen").

motion.name: card-flip
motion.value: ScrollTrigger pin on .opening, end +=100%, scrub 0.5; one progress p rendered into CSS variables
motion.purpose: 0-0.12 lines under the card step aside; 0-0.42 card turns 180deg (power1.inOut) and swells to 1.12; 0.45-0.75 back grows to fill the screen (power2.in); at 0.75 card and desk vanish over the pinned cover; 0.76-0.96 the cover title prints in.

motion.name: scroll-print
motion.purpose: Section titles: --print rolls a clip-path, --mis-x slides the red pass from -18px to 3px. Reverses on the way up.

motion.name: tail-flick
motion.purpose: The cat on the riddle card flicks its tail when the card comes into view.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion everything shows its final state: no hand-over, no pin, no flip; card and cover are plain sections.

narrative.overview:
The page is a self-published zine, printed on a riso in two inks, and it is handed to you as a name card first. Each release is an issue (v1.0.0 was Issue 1, v1.1.0 is Issue 2; a patch is a reprint). The opening is a meishi (91 × 55) lying on a desk: it rises into your hand on load, and as you scroll it turns over, its back grows across the screen and becomes the zine's cover. From there the zine reads as before: a masthead with the title, the contents and which print you hold; a cover that sells the issue with cover lines and page numbers; spreads of two pages split by a hairline gutter and numbered with folios; a back page with contact and the riddle; and a hidden centrefold that opens when the riddle is solved.

Two inks do all the work: a dark graphite grey (pale grey in the night print) and a red. The red pass never lines up perfectly with the grey, so headings carry a few pixels of misregistration. A lighter grey is the third tone, for fields, rules, halftones and the desk. The stock is near white by day and dark grey by night, with one static layer of grain so it reads as printed rather than rendered. Nothing is distressed. Type is wide and heavy for headings and a bookish serif for reading.

Provenance: the zine world replaced the seeded isometric-building world at v1.0.0 (2026-11-18; see `docs/decisions/0002-riso-zine-redesign.md`). It came from direction roll `seed:e4c83ff7a6b64abf`, which ran degraded (the style catalog was unreachable from the cloud session, so there were no challengers). Issue 2 (v1.1.0) extended that world rather than replacing it: it added the name card opening and changed the inks from riso blue and sunflower to graphite and red (see `docs/decisions/0003-name-card-and-new-inks.md`). It is a code-led build with no comps, so this file is the record of what shipped. Because the world replaced the seeded one, no `world:` provenance is carried.
keyCharacteristics: Two inks only: graphite (pale grey at night) and red, plus a lighter grey and the paper.
Misregistration on titles and the card name, done as a `text-shadow`, one copy of the text.
Square everything: no radius anywhere, the name card included.
Print furniture as structure: a name card, masthead, cover lines with page numbers, folios, a dashed trim line between spreads, staples on the centrefold.
One automatic motion: the card handed over on load. The card flip and the section titles follow the scroll.

rules.name: The Two Drums Rule
rules.body: Every colour is one of the two inks, a tint of the grey (halftone, rule, muted, desk), or the paper. A third hue breaks the print.

rules.name: The Red Text Rule
rules.body: Red is text only where it reaches 4.5:1 on its ground (the card's contact labels on paper). Everywhere else red is a fill, an underline or a shadow, and any text on a red fill uses `--on-accent`.

rules.name: The Token-Only Rule
rules.body: Components take colours from the tokens. The grain's neutral grey inside its SVG filter is the only literal colour, and it is blended, not seen.

rules.name: The Wide Not Tall Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy comes from Anybody's width and weight axes first. Headings are set wide (105 to 140), never condensed.

rules.name: The Mono Is Code Rule
rules.body: Monospace appears only for code. Labels, dates, values and file names use Anybody.

rules.name: The Overprint Rule
rules.body: Depth on the page is ink on ink. Shadows there only exist as the second ink pass, an inset outline, or a paper fold.

rules.name: The One Object Rule
rules.body: Only the name card lifts off its surface. Spreads, panels, the riddle card and the masthead stay flat on the sheet.

rules.name: The One Copy Rule
rules.body: Effects never duplicate text. Find-in-page and copy see one copy.

dos: Do take every colour from the tokens and check both prints.
Do keep to two inks: graphite (pale grey at night) and red, plus the lighter grey tints and the paper.
Do put red behind text, under text or beside it, and set any text on a red fill in `--on-accent`.
Do make misregistration with `text-shadow` on one copy of the text, offset by `--mis-x` and `--mis-y`.
Do use print furniture for structure: the name card, cover lines with page numbers, folios, trim lines, page gutters.
Do draw numbers to scale, with the production result in red and baselines or test data in halftone.
Do keep every corner square and every touch target at 44px or more.
Do drive scroll motion with one value rendered into CSS variables, so hover, focus, `:target` and reduced motion keep working and the page looks finished without GSAP.
Do let motion answer the user, apart from the hand-over on load, and show final states under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
donts: Don't set red text on paper below 4.5:1.
Don't duplicate text to fake a second ink pass.
Don't add a third hue, a gradient sky, or a glow.
Don't distress the paper: one static grain layer, no torn edges or fake grunge.
Don't round corners, and don't give any container but the name card a drop shadow.
Don't show the Azbil logo; the organisation is text.
Don't use monospace for labels, dates or values; it is for code only.
Don't add automatic motion beyond the hand-over.
Don't let the test-data strip outweigh production results.
